$comment: Tools/Simulate. Everything the 50,000-match run needs that is not already
in seed.json (the population) or redline.economy.json (the rules).
The split matters: rules the SERVER enforces live in the economy config and
the simulation reads the same file, so a reviewer changing the rake or the
matchmaking band changes both at once. Only things that exist purely for
$seed: Drives arrivals and outcomes. Independent of seed.json's, so the same population can be run under different luck.
$startTime: The virtual timeline's origin. Nothing in the run reads the wall clock.
$maxVirtualDays: A stop so a misconfigured activity profile cannot run forever. Reaching it before targetMatches is a failure the harness reports rather than hides.

outcome.$comment: How skill and greed become a banked score. See OutcomeModel for the formulas.
outcome.$scoreScale: Expected reachable score for a player at referenceSkill. Arbitrary units — only ratios matter, since the winner is whoever banked more.
outcome.$referenceSkill: Must equal rating.initial and seed.json's latentSkill.mean, so capability 1.0 sits at the middle of the population.
outcome.$safety: How much further than their target a player can typically go. This is the term that makes skill lower the crash rate instead of only raising the score: at 400, a player one whole reference-skill above average survives 40% further.
outcome.$riskFraction: Where greed puts the banking target, as a fraction of capability. The timid bank at a quarter of what they could reach; the greedy drive half again past it and crash most of the time.
outcome.$throwFraction: What a thrown match banks. Small but not zero — an anomaly that scored exactly zero every time would be caught by a rule so crude that catching it would prove nothing about the detector.

output.$why: CSV, one row per match, written as the run goes. The report must be regenerable from these files without re-running the simulation.
